utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please be seated. So Madam registrar, yes. Madam registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours and good morning to the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, counsel for the Prosecution, together with co-counsel, Ms. Patricia Sellers and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, together with Mr. John Jones, I appear on behalf of Mr. Naser Oric. We have with us today our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts. Good morning also to my learned friends from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you as well and your team. Before I ask if you have any preliminaries, my secretary has drawn my attention, actually, that these photos that you handed sometime back a few -- I think sometime last week, to form part of Dr. Stankovic's report, do not have a number. They do have an ERN number. How would you like us to have them filed and recorded?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, part of our question was whether we could hand them up to you to say that these are merely colour photos of what you have or would you prefer that this go through the registrar as a submission of filing. If it does, they will photocopy them and the colour photos will again become black and white photos. That's what happened the first time. That's why we tried to avoid that by handing that up. I don't know whether there could be a disconsultation from the registrar not to photocopy four copies of them, the ones that we distribute, or whether we can use that as a submission that you look at to understand just the contents of what's been filed. I put myself in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words do I take it, Ms. Sellers, that the ERN number that is shown here on each of these four pages, corresponds to the ERN number on the black and white?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, it does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Then can we substitute or just insert them next to where we have the black and white ones, without giving these any specific number? Can you live with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I think that is what we've done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. Definitely there is a difference between coloured photos and black and white photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It's fine with us, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We thank you for that practical solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. [Trial Chamber confers with registrar].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So any preliminaries before ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One minor thing that I wanted to raise. We will stop on Wednesday, as you know and then we will resume on the 4th when we are supposed to have a video link. If there are problems with the video link, in the meantime, between now and then, please do let us know, particularly us and of course the Defence. I mean I know that you definitely will let the Defence know before you will let us know. But we would also like to be alerted should that be the case and also be informed of what the alternatives are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We will provide you with the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, let's wait for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to proceed with your cross-examination today. I don't take it that we will finish today, but we will do our utmost to finish tomorrow, and then you can go back home. Please take a seat. You are still testifying under oath, in terms of your solemn declaration. And may I just remind you to allow an interval of time between question and answer so that you do not create problems to the interpreters. Yes, Madam Vidovic. You may proceed. Cross-examined by Ms. Vidovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday in your testimony that while you worked as a police officer during the war, you heard many accounts by Muslim refugees who reached Srebrenica, did you not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is true that their accounts indicated that the same principle of persecuting Muslims applied as that used by the SDS in east Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next thing would be a call to the local -- by the local Serb authorities for the Muslims to hand over their weapons. People would mostly comply. The next thing would be shelling and then an infantry attack where the local Serbs would join in usually. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Arson, looting, murder. These were not crimes perpetrated by some other soldiers of the army of Republika Srpska. None other in fact than the local population reinforced by volunteers from Serbia as well as the military and paramilitary units arriving from Serbia, is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what's your objection? I think I know what it is but let me hear it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe that this witness has testified that he had specifically spoken to people who said that. I don't know whether this witness can testify to these patterns. I believe that he is being presented a series of actually statements and he is merely saying, yes. In terms of whether the local Serbs Republika Srpska army, I do not believe that we've ever elicited that to his knowledge. On the other hand, I would say that I understand some of these issues might have been raised during his direct examination. I do not believe at this point that that is completely the extent to which we're going into it is relevant to the issues beforehand, but I do understand that, yes, he did talk about some refugees coming in. I just want to clarify that for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. In fact certain issues that you raised are very valid although not all. I hand in mind actually of interrupting Ms. -- Madam Vidovic at a certain time arising out of a question that she asked and then the witness answered and I will do that first. You were asked, Witness, to draw a comparison between what was happening in the vicinity, according to what you were being told by refugees coming to Srebrenica, to what happened in eastern Bosnia. What do you know about what happened in eastern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on the accounts of refugees upon their arrival, we obtained information. We were told what had happened. Those were refugees from the Visegrad area, the ones that we had in Srebrenica as well as those from Rogatica, Han Pijesak and Bratunac and Zvornik too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is not eastern Bosnia though, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it should be, that is the Podravanje area, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, that would be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may of assistance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You consider it to be eastern Bosnia. The next question that you were asked by Madam Vidovic, this seems to distinguish between the involvement of Republika Srpska army, the involvement of the local citizens and inhabitants and the involvement of the Serbian army. I do understand that this is relevant, in terms of some of the evidence that we heard recently, but also before. We need to dissect it however, Ms. -- Madam Vidovic because the way you put it can only ask for a confusionary answer or an answer which will not be convincing to start with.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will try to rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, it's true, isn't it, that the local Serb population was involved in the burnings, lootings and killings in the Podravanje area.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may use a piece of information that I obtained from a lady citizen in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You may do so.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to her and she said that she had received word that her house would be set on fire. She went to the police station. She found a duty officer who was an acquaintance of hers, a neighbour of hers, was the chief of the Serb police station. She asked why her house would be burned and he said, Wait a minute. He looked through a notebook and he said, Your house is not on the list. As some houses were burned and some were skipped or spared, I think lists were drawn up with peoples first and last names. And this was determined on the basis of indications provided by a local.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, Mr. Bogilovic, are you saying that the local Serb population was also involved in the burnings, lootings and killings of the Muslim population of Podravanja? The time frame is April and May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Quite correct. I'm talking more about Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that in doing so, the local population was assisted by volunteers from Serbia and various paramilitary and military formations arriving from Serbia itself. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that on the 18th of April, 1992, Serb units came in. One unit, they referred to it as a company, was billeted at the Domadia Hotel and led by a man name Pero Zemunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Question. This man, Pero Zemunac, was a volunteer from Serbia, was he not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know him, but that's what they said about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The assertion that the local Serbian population of Srebrenica and Bratunac were merely trying to preserve their own villages throughout 1992 and early 1993 based on your own experience. Based on what you learned and heard from other people, this would in fact not be true, would it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it wouldn't. I was on the train when I found out that everything would be sorted in a matter of 15 days. There was an experienced team coming in led by captain Dragan and Arkan. They said new authorities would be set up within 15 days and there would be peace. However then the burnings and lootings ensued and people started feeling very afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, you didn't answer my question, in fact. What I was talking about was the local Serb population. The assertion or the theory that the local Serb population of the Srebrenica and Bratunac areas were merely guarding their villages throughout 1992 and early 1993. Based on what you know about this, this assertion would in fact not be true, would it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not. If everyone was just guarding their own house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The theory that the local inhabitants of Skelani, back in 1992, and you were in the area of April 1992, were you not? So the theory that all they had were village guards or village watches would also not be true, would it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Village guards, no. When I was passing through, there was a military presence there with a barracks at Jezero.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that in early April both Serbs and Muslims left Srebrenica due to tensions that prevailed in the area. As concerns Srebrenica itself, it is true, isn't it, that Serbs in fact occupied Srebrenica in mid April 1992, did they not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were negotiations in mid April and Srebrenica was finally evacuated on the 17th or rather 18th of April. Alija Hasic left Srebrenica at 10 o'clock sharp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that Serbs entered Srebrenica after that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 17th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your testimony on Friday, you said that many of the Muslims who remained behind burned some houses, in fact, around eighty houses including your own. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, burned houses. Killed an entire family including children and the remaining people were elderly people, or people who were already retired. There was a man and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Are we talking of Muslims burning houses? Or is it a mistake?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my question was: During your testimony on Friday you said that many of the Muslims who remained behind were burned by the Serbs and, in fact, burned about 80 of their houses including your own. Isn't that true, Mr. Bogilovic, that the Serbs burned down 88 Muslim houses and killed many of the Muslims who stayed behind in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's true. I believe a total of seven or eight families they burned down -- the houses burned down. That's how they were found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So just for the record, I want to make sure that this is clear. Lines 16 to 18 on page 9, your question as reported in the transcript is wrong here. You asked supposedly according to the transcript, you asked the witness: During your testimony on Friday, you said that many of the Muslims who remained behind burned some houses. In fact, around eighty houses including your own. Isn't that true? And his answer is: Yes, burned houses. Killed an entire family including children and the remaining people were elderly, et cetera. So taken together these -- this question and answer mean exactly the opposite of what you wanted to prove and what I understand the witness is telling. But that is just for the record, okay, I'm making it clear. Yes, please proceed and don't worry about it any longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the Serbs left the town following Goran Zekic's death, in their wake, they left devastation, did they not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They took with them everything of any value at all, did they not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Word had it that Arkan's units, liberating the area from the Muslim units, would be granted 2000 German marks as a reward and that they would be entitled to take all electrical appliances away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Srebrenica's public institutions were laid waste to as well, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the factories, everything was taken away. The secondary school headmaster took a computer away for his own personal use in Bajina Basta from the school that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Serbs took everything that might have been used for work, for production, documents, type writers too, you said?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The police station had been demolished too; right?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you reached Srebrenica, after the Serb's departure, you found nothing there that could be used to conduct police or criminal investigations, carry out on-site inspections, that sort of thing, forensic work in general.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite right. Everything had been smashed, destroyed, taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Experts of war crimes left Srebrenica, isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Starting with the typewriter and all the way to doctors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those who were left behind were people who had lost their bearings and refugees flooding in from all sides into Srebrenica as early as May, 1992 and on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only educated people were those from the country who took refuge in the country and it is quite true that the remaining people there were quite uneducated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Refugees were arriving in Srebrenica with dreadful hair-raising stories about crimes, were they not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This caused a lot of fear and panic, did it not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bogilovic, it's true, isn't it, that far too many people were crammed in the small space that was Srebrenica as early as June 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The people from Bratunac had fled to the woods, the people from Skelani, the people from Vlasenica, most of them headed for Suceska but some came to Srebrenica too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore the same situation applied in Suceska and other Muslim villages that had not been taken yet with floods of refugees coming in?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As people were attacked, people would run and would draw to the next village, spend a day or two there, but then they would walk on and most of them would come to Srebrenica, would end up in Srebrenica eventually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bogilovic. From the day the Muslims returned to Srebrenica, the attacks of the Serb forces from the surrounding villages who were receiving support from Serbia itself, or rather, perhaps, I should rephrase my question. There ensued attacks by the Serb forces from the surrounding Serb villages, attacks against the Srebrenica area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fiercest attacks were carried out Friday afternoon, Saturday all day long and Sunday afternoon. The specials came, special units and they shelled the town. You had to run and hide in those days. The remaining days, when there was shelling, it wasn't safe, so people moved about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, the population of Srebrenica and other Muslim enclaves were subjected to shelling on a daily basis. However, on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, the shelling grew in intensity, is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were frequent air attacks too, air strikes, were there not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were these planes that we referred to as boilers, rather small planes, carrying boilers filled with explosives that would then be dropped on the town. There were fast planes too. You hear it coming, but you can hardly see. That's how fast they were. Fighter planes. There were quite a number of helicopters too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The helicopters in fact raid the Srebrenica area and the Muslim villages with machine-gun fire, did they not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But sometimes they would just fly over without doing anything. Sometimes one, sometimes two, sometimes three, they were dropping leaflets all the while though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, please allow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please allow an interval between question and answer because you are going too fast, both of you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were frequent infantry attacks on Srebrenica and the surrounding Muslim villages, were there not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the attack on Bratunac, their territory spread and they went and attacked our villages one by one. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Muslim villages were isolated and they were crisscrossed with the Serbian settlements and Serbian military strongholds; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because Muslim and Serb villages --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: At this point, we do not have any time frame that we are speaking about. I certainly believe that at one point that Madam Vidovic was referring specifically to when Mr. Bogilovic was a police officer. And then another point of time I thought we were speaking about April and May. It seems now that we have moved into a timeless zone and therefore I would state an objection. It is not clear. I would also like to state that during his direct testimony, we did not lead any evidence of that in a time period after the May 20th meeting. So therefore I don't think it is part of our direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The objection is valid on both counts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your Honour, I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, it's correct, is it not, that during 1992 -- I'm referring to the time from the beginning of the war in 1992 until the demilitarisation in 1993, the Muslim villages were isolated and they were interrupted with -- by Serbian villages and Serbian military strongholds.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will phrase my question differently, Mr. Bogilovic. It's correct, is it not, that throughout 1992 - I'm referring to the period of the war - and the beginning of 1993, up to the demilitarisation, Srebrenica itself was cut off to a large extent from the other small Muslim enclaves and villages. In other words, their mutual links between Srebrenica and these villages were very poor. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because Srebrenica was isolated, communication was by courier. This was difficult. The courier would go and never come back and, in time, this territory became more extensive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was, therefore, very dangerous for couriers to move between Srebrenica and other Muslim villages, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But there was no other means of communication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just as a matter of clarification. We already asked you that you state the time frame within which you are talking. But now we are also coming to localities. It would be, I think, quite important to know when he -- you speak of other small Muslim enclaves and villages, what villages you are thinking of. Are they villages directly around Srebrenica? Or are you thinking of villages such as Kravica or Skelani or do they include villages within your description? And another point would be that you would, perhaps, tell us what you know by having seen it yourself or what you know by having been told from others. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This referred to the villages near Srebrenica and around Srebrenica. The other villages you have mentioned were far from Srebrenica. I'm referring to Kravica, Skelani and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But could you mention some of the villages around Srebrenica you are thinking of? Give some names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bajramovici, Pusmulici, Likari, for a time the road to Potocari was cut off and then the communication was reestablished.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, it's true, is it not, that villages such as Osmace, Kragljivoda, Pirici were cut off and it was not easy to reach these villages?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It was not easy to reach them, because the Serb forces had cut them off.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]: Thank you very much. I would now like to ask the usher for assistance. Can the witness be shown Exhibit P73. This is a decision of the 20th of May, 1992 from Bajramovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, you have already testified about this decision and you confirmed that these seven people, whose names are listed in the decision, entered the staff and then another three men did. These are Oric from Potocari, Ustic from Srebrenica, Tursonovic, Zulfo and you from Suceska, Fasic Hamdija from Bajramovici, Sefket Dozic from Bojna, Ahmo Tihic from Jelesce and later on Akif Krdzic from Osmace, Nedzad Bektic from Caracici and Senahid Tabakovic from Skanderovici. This was the additional decision you don't have before you. This is correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But in this format then at that time -- no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have never seen this decision before, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness's response?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Neither did I. What was your answer to Madam Vidovic's question whether you had seen this document, I take it, P73, no? Whether you had seen this document before? What is your answer to that question, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never saw it until the Prosecutors of this court showed it to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic. It's true, is it not, that there were many other villages in the area of Srebrenica and Bratunac which had their armed groups and which were not present at the meeting in Bajramovici at all; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's true. The meeting in Bajramovici was attended only by this team and that was a group that were closest to each other. All the other teams were far away and they didn't even know about it. Every village had its own group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Moreover, many people in these other villages didn't even know about the agreement in Bajramovici?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew the area of Suceska well. And you knew its commanders Zulfo Tursonovic. During your testimony, you told us that you were there until July 1992; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I was appointed on the 20th of May, 1992 and I returned from Bajramovici to collect my things. Several days later I returned to Srebrenica to take up the job I had been assigned to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that the witness's testimony on direct was more that he had remained in Suceska until toward the end of May. Maybe if we could just have that clarified. Not July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. When did you leave Suceska, Mr. Bogilovic? Do you remember the exact date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't recall the exact date. I had to go back to see about my chickens and my things and my accommodation was uncertain down there, so that some days passed but I apologise, I cannot tell you the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However that may be, Mr. Bogilovic, you were familiar with the situation in Suceska until July, 1992 at least. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not until July, because throughout June I was in Srebrenica. At the beginning I was in Suceska the whole time, so, yes, I was familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I will now ask you the following. It's correct, is it not, that in Suceska, when the war broke out, while you were there, there were armed groups of refugees from Vlasenica under the command of Becir Mekanic and Fadil Turkovic and they were not under the command of Zulfo Tursonovic at all. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even know Becir. Later on, in Tuzla I learned about him. I knew Fadil, that was a different area and a different municipality. Fadil was active on the other side, not on the territory of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, I didn't ask you about the area of Srebrenica. It's correct, is it not, that on the broader territory of Suceska, apparent from Zulfo Tursunovic's unit, in May and June 1992, there were other units fighting, units commanded by Fadil Turkovic and Becir Mekanic. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of Fadil, not the other one, Becir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. These units never entered the composition of the armed forces of Srebrenica, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that these units participated in the fighting around Podravanja?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that these units, also with respect to the refugees from Vlasenica, tried to provide food for them. They tried to provide weapons for themselves and that they took part in fighting for food and weapons with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of what their units did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you don't know that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct, is it not, that these units had no connection with Srebrenica and Oric?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I find it to be a bit of a non-sequiter. If he doesn't know anything about the units in and of themselves, he doesn't know whether they have a connection or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Isn't that a conclusion to be drawn by whoever needs to make decisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. I just like to bring what seems to be quite an illogical conclusion from the sequence of questions now on the record now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not going to interfere in this, Madam Vidovic. Go ahead with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness said he knew about Fadil Turkovic's unit. I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, it's correct, isn't it, that there were armed groups of Muslims in Poznanovici, Dedici, Podkorijen, Mocevici, and Brezovice which at least until mid October --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because Judge Eser is raising something which is important, according to me. I think we ought to have a map available at this stage, because we are finding it difficult to follow. There are several maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The thing is -- the problem arose because my suggestion to the Prosecution was not followed in the case of this witness. My suggestion was to have a map available.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do have maps. The reason we didn't have one with this witness is as a matter of fact our testimony of this witness was very much located in the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But let's choose a map and have it on the ELMO and, from time to time, the witness may be required to indicate where these places are so that at least, relative to Srebrenica we would know where we are. I think this map that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me see. I may have one here. C1. See if you have a C1 map, with just C1. C1. It's marked C, because it is a court document. Yes, let's use this one. Usher, come near me, and I will explain to you which part you need to put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we pulled one up on Sanctions, if you would like to look at it and see if this would be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But would we be able to move up and down the map on Sanction? Because I don't think we will.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No. Only if the radius -- if you would look at your Sanctions now if that would be a map that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Leave it on Sanction too, but for the time being, I think is it wiser if we use this one. Put this on the ELMO for the time being, centering -- focussing on Srebrenica and then we move as it becomes necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am asking about the Ratkovici area, if I can assist the witness. Would you please look at the area around Radosevici and Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I see here is the centre of Srebrenica and the villages close to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you see Ratkovici and Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. This is a narrow area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, could you please press computer evidence, the computer evidence button for the witness, please. There is a coloured map there, Mr. Bogilovic. And you will see that roughly just to the east of Srebrenica, there is Ratkovici and Fakovici and to the west of Srebrenica there is Suceska.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So keep concentrating on that map as we go along. Yes, Madam Vidovic and we will see what we can make of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't think he can actually see it on this coloured map. I would prefer to use the other one, if it shows the Ratkovici area, which I am not certain about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you bring it over. I will show you which part you need to put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see some of the villages on this map. I can see Mocevici, Brezovice?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see Mocevici too, Brezovice, Sobin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please look at Poznanovici, Dedici and Podkorijen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Poznanovici, Dedici and Podkorijen are below Ratkovici. If you could have a look, please, you can see it on the map?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But on the other side towards Bratunac, the -- across the hills I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, may I proceed with this? Can you please use the pointer now, Mr. Bogilovic, to show these villages, Poznanovici, Dedici and Podkorijen there just below Ratkovici. Some centimetres further down going from Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Poznanovici, here it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes for the record, the witness indicates to the village of Podnanovici on the map, which is two grids below Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, Mr. Bogilovic, that Dedici and Podkorijen are Muslim villages in the vicinity of Poznanovici? I'm not actually sure we can see those on the map. I'm not sure if you can, can you? But you do agree with me when I say that these are villages close to Poznanovici?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an area known as Poznanovici, with hamlet's, small villages Dedici and Podkorijen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Can you please show Mocevici and Brezovice on the map. You did see them a while ago, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mocevici right here and Brezovice, a bit further in this direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness indicates with a pointer to the two villages of Mocevici and Brezovice which are two and four grids above Dedici respectively. Yes, Brezovice and Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question about this. It's true, isn't it, that in these Muslim villages too, there were armed groups whose members were not present at the meeting in Bajramovici, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true. They weren't present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's also true that at least until as late as mid October, those groups acted on their own?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the date, but they were far from us and we had nothing to do with them, especially me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When about your information, did these units too try to defend themselves from the Serbs, seize their weapons, get food for the refugees?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I believe each and every one of these villages got themselves organised for fear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. The question went beyond the concept of fear, I think. The question was: When about your information, did these units too try to defend themselves from the Serbs? And there you need to answer the question: "Seize their weapons and get food for the refugees". So it's a question of defence. It's a question of obtaining weapons and, thirdly, of obtaining food and food specifically for refugees. Did your information fill or satisfy all of these three points? Let's take them one by one. The information that you had, sir, were these units trying to defend themselves from the Serbs as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on the information that I received, some of those who came said that all the villages were getting themselves organised, helping each other out, and every time an attack occurred by the Serb units, they tried to defend themselves. I don't know what sort of internal organisation they had, because I was never in the area throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you also receive information that these units were trying to obtain weapons from the Serbs, seize weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I heard said, they found those because earlier there had been people saying that the Serbs had quite a number of weapons. When we entered Srebrenica, we found large caches of weapons in houses with only one owner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the information that you were receiving, sir, was it also to the extent that those units were getting food for refugees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I didn't know about that. But they had to feed them, didn't they, those who kept coming in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a conclusion. Yes. Madam Vidovic, sorry to have interrupted you like that but I think we needed to clear this, because there were three things put together in one question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Mr. Bogilovic, these units had their own local commanders. Was this something you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it was only later that one learned who the commanders had been or team leaders if you like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of a man named Vekaz Husic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later on. I think he's from Mocevici, isn't he? I think so at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, when you say we only found out later, this means that in the first months of war, you, people in the leading positions in Srebrenica, had no contact whatsoever with these local commanders, does it not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that I saw none of these commanders at the time. I don't know whether anyone else did, but this was quite far from us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, therefore, that they did not come to Srebrenica for meetings. You never saw any of them in Srebrenica, did you?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not in those days when we were getting ourselves organised in May, June and July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that the refugees from the Bratunac area, especially those from Glogova, tried to get themselves organised on their own in order to return to their village?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's true. A man named Golic was referred to in this context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you something about that too. You mentioned Ejub Golic. You probably had Ejub Golic in mind, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that a Ejub Golic had a large armed group of people over in Cizmici, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once they had fled Glogova, that was the first village they came across. It is also part of Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please now go back to the map and show the Trial Chamber the villages of Vojevica, Biljaca and Zaluzje. That is the area around Bratunac. Can you please pull the map up a little. Can you please show Vojevica, Biljaca and Zaluzje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness indicates with the pointer on the map the village of Vojevica and the village of Zaluzje which are -- can you move the -- which are two grids and four and -- three grids below Ljubovija on the map, to the east of Bratunac. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Biljaca is even further down, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The witness indicates to the village of Biljaca which is two grids below Zaluzje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout 1992, and obviously, Mr. Bogilovic, I'm referring to the war period, refugees from these villages also had armed groups which they used to try and return to their homes and, in fact, they fought, the local Serbs didn't they?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The civilians had fled to the woods and then they came to Srebrenica and they were the first to arrive, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that a large number of civilians and other people remained in the nearby woods?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were substantial groups of people, in fact, that were not present at the meeting in Bajramovici on the 25th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, the decision to set up a Srebrenica staff did not refer to them, did it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to show the witness P4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: P4 is an order to the local commanders of self-organised armed groups dated the 15th of July, 1992 -- of June, interpreter's correction, 15th of June. Mr. Bogilovic, you were shown this document by the Prosecutor but can we please go through this again and have a good look, please. Based on this, that's if the document is authentic at all, one could conclude that on the 15th of June, 1992, there were, in fact, local commanders of self-organised armed groups and these commanders were requested to start organising immediately. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The names that I see here, these persons were chosen or selected by the people of these villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you therefore agree that on the 15th of June, if this document is anything to go by, they were ordered to start organising and establishing units immediately?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should be, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what the document says, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we please go back to these ten names, or rather, nine names stated here. Can you please look at the names from 1 to 10, the names -- or rather, the villages referred to in this document, if you can have a look, please. My next question will be about that. It's true, isn't it that the armed groups that I asked you about a while ago, namely those from Vlasenica, Poznanovici, Mocevici, Brezovice, Glogova, Vojevica, Zalulje and Biljaca were not, in fact, included in this order? Were they?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic. That will be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Vidovic. I am of course looking at the English version and not the B/C/S one. But before we come to the list starting with number 1, that is the word, at least in the English language, "in particular", which would qualify your statement or your question. The correct way of presenting it is: Is it correct that the other villages that you mentioned are not listed. But I don't think you can ask whether they are included or not, because it only says "in particular."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So they are not listed and you can, of course, ask for a confirmation of that, but you --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you want to ask the other question whether they were included, then you have to be very specific. In other words, you would need to ask the question whether this would mean that those were definitely not included. Were excluded, in other words. Or not included.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it seems that this is a misinterpretation, because this order in Bosnian does not contain this --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mistranslation. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will read the first part of the order. Would the interpreters please follow and could the usher please put this on the ELMO. This word especially does not exist. What it says here is "e tor," meaning "and that." I will read it out. "Order. All local commanders of self-organised armed groups with a view to opposing the aggressors and carry out a war of liberation for the return of occupied areas are ordered to immediately start organisational and formational establishment of units of the Srebrenica Territorial Defence as follows:"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But "as follows" is something which is completely different to what I read out in the English version, so it is a good thing that I mentioned it, that I brought this up, because it does make a difference. All right. I thank you, so I will not raise the matter -- pursue the matter any further. You need not put any further questions to the witness on the issue that I raised. It's clear enough. But this is the problem when you have --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the problem that you have when you have translations. "As follows." Because "as follows" is completely different from "in particular." Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, even in Srebrenica itself, there was a large group of armed people under the command of Hakija Meholjic and Naser Oric had no influence over that group. Is this in accordance with what you know?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now show the witness P80. This document was allegedly issued by the Srebrenica staff of the 19th of September, 1993 and its the delivery of information with respect to the establishment of armed forces in Srebrenica in the past period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First, would you please look through these three pages. You will see that the first establishment of formation is mentioned and the date is the 20th of May, 1992. Mr. Bogilovic, would you please look at page 1. The first formation structure and the date is the 20th of May, 1992. And then the second formation structure, the date is the 3rd of September. And then, if you will turn the page, to 02075845, that's the third page, you will see the third paragraph begins on the 14th of October, 1992. Pursuant to an order from the command a reorganisation has been carried out. This is the 14th of October, 1992. Would you now turn to page 4, which I will ask you about. The number is 02075846. Would you now, please, pay attention to what it says here under 4. Would you please look at it and I will quote. "The independent Srebrenica battalion with its headquarters in Srebrenica. Commander Safet Mujic. 849 conscripts. Composition five companies. The first company with its headquarters in the Stari Grad. Commander Enes Ustic. Second company, headquarters Solocusa. Commander Hebibovic Ramiz. Third company, headquarters in Kazani. Commander Suad Smailovic. Fourth company, headquarters Bajramovici" -- thank you. I apologise. "Fourth company, headquarters in Bajramovici. Commander Sabahudin Jusic. Fifth company, headquarters in Srebrenica. Commander Hakija Meholjic." Mr. Bogilovic, I have just asked you about Mr. Meholjic. It's true, is it not, that Safet Mujic was never the commander of Hakija Meholjic? Nor was Meholic's unit part of the Srebrenica TO.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards Hakija Meholjic, he would certainly have never agreed for Safet Mujic to be his superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore -- this is something that is written down on paper. In fact, in real life, in Srebrenica, in 1992 and 1993, this was not how it was; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout this time Hakija waged a policy of his own. He refused to participate while Hakib was alive. He negotiated with him about something, I don't know what. But as for military matters, I wasn't there and I can't tell you about that. I know that they were there and that they had an escort, a bodyguard to protect them, both of them, and I found this ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, it's correct, is it not, that Hakija Meholjic was never under the command of Mr. Safet Mujic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know for certain or rather I don't know that he was ever under Safet Mujic's command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mr. Bogilovic, would you now please look at what it says under number five. This is an independent battalion, Skenderovici. Its headquarters is in Skenderovici. And then companies are listed: The first company based in Stozersko. Second company based in Mocevici. Third company based in Brezovice. Fourth company based in Poloznik. Independent platoon based in Zapolje, sabotage and reconnaissance platoon. Do you agree, in view of the fact that this is the second formation structure and that its date is the 14th of October, 1992, that even from this document it follows that the men from the -- from Stozersko, Brezovice, Poloznik and Zapolje were not part of the Skenderovici unit before the 14th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly agree with that. It could not have been one unit because they were cut off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Let us go back for a moment, Mr. Bogilovic, to the first page of this document where it says "first formation structure." And I will quote what it says here under the heading "first formation structure." It says: "On the 20th of May, 1992, in Bajramovici, the Srebrenica -- the Srebrenica Territorial Defence staff was formed. From the 17th of April, 1992 to mid-October, 1992 the first regional units were formed under the auspices of the TO, namely TO Potocari, TO Suceska, Grabivoda, Skenderovici, Srebrenica, Luca." Mr. Bogilovic, my question is as follows: It's correct, is it not, that these units were not established at the same time and that the process of their establishment stretched over a protracted time period. The document itself says from the 17th of April 1992 to mid-October, 1992. Is this in accordance with what you know?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the first formation was on the 25th, Srebrenica and the nearby villages, Bajramovici, Potocari, the ones I mentioned, because you couldn't communicate with the people in the other villages. You couldn't reach them. And as time went by, things were protracted in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic. It would be wrong to conclude that they were all formed on the 25th of May, 1992 in Bajramovici. Or let us say the 15th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course it would be wrong because the first date -- what was done on the area of Bratunac and Vlasenica and the people were afraid and the first meeting was on the 25th of May, 1992, but that was only Suceska, Potocari and Bajramovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It's correct, is it not, that in general resistance to the Serb persecution was offered only by organised groups scattered around individuals, including Oric?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The actions that followed were a reflection of the looting. In order to prevent that, there were actions in Potocari and Osmace. Those are the actions I know about. And there was one in Suceska when they said that all the workers should come to us and work. And when they arrived there, they were arrested and detained. Then the team at Zutica, which is the area of Vlasenica, and for the most part they worked in the mine, they blocked the road and took five vehicles of bauxite. And then there was an exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Hold it. Hold it. Because sometimes matters tend to get out of hand completely. I don't see how this fits in in any way the question Madam Vidovic put to you. It was a very simple question to you, Mr. Bogilovic. The question was: Is it correct, it's correct, is it not, that in general resistance to the Serb persecution was offered only by organised groups, scattered-around individuals, including Oric. Your answer did not cover that question. It covered other things, but not that question. So perhaps you could answer, answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will reply to the question. Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Eser has a question for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: You mentioned "the actions that followed were a reflection of the looting." What actions are you referring to? Actions by whom? And looting by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serb forces were looting. They were taking away technical goods, the property belonging to companies and enterprises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And before you speak of looting you would say the actions that followed were a reflection of the looting, but not -- what did you mean with "actions"? Actions of whom, by whom? Taken by whom? Actions taken by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These actions were taken by the local villagers, the local inhabitants of the villages. Because they wanted to keep the factories there. They were working in those factories. They didn't want the machines to be taken away. So they blocked the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Madam Vidovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this might be a very good time, because I have now rounded off this topic. So it might be a good time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a 25-minute minute break starting from now. Thank you. Are you on schedule, you think?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I believe so. There are documents to follow, but I think I will be able to complete as scheduled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry for the delay, but something came up on the way to the courtroom and -- which I had to deal with, about other cases, of course, not this one. Yes, Madam Vidovic, you may proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, what happened in Bajramovici, the decision that was made to set up the so-called Srebrenica staff, you spoke about that. This decision was taken in Bajramovici by an informal group of people, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a group of people in Bajramovici, representatives of those groups from Bajramovici had Hambija from Suceska Zulfo and from Potocari, Oric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So this decision was not taken by the socio-political community or another body that would be in charge of anything like that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The community could not have taken that decision because the community had left Srebrenica by this time and there were no authorities in place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Given the fact that the decision was made by an informal group of people, the decision was not complied with by all armed groups and individuals, was it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite right, but it depends on the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that the only criterion to become a member of the staff that was appointed in Bajramovici was a contribution in terms of resistance, is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the people chose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was -- no qualifications were not a consideration at the time, were they?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because there were no qualified people around.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to place the following document on the ELMO. The document is from the Pobudje territorial defence dated the 6th of June, 1992 and the number is 01838973.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please have a look. The date, or rather, the heading is: "Pobudje TO, 6th of June, 1992". And then it says, "Surrender to Susnjari TO/Slatina TO or Potocari TO, or possibly deliver to Susnjari/Slatina or Potocari TO". I will quote one portion of this document, the first portion. I quote, "The other day, if there had been cooperation and agreement between us, we would have managed to come together and embark on 'mopping up' Rogac and beyond towards Milici". "We subsequently carried out actions in a different part of the field, so we had no time to send a messenger to you. We are holding firmly all the positions in our area, although there was a misunderstanding with Urkovici, and we abandoned the areas that we had previously taken. To avoid any future misunderstandings and in order to ensure closer cooperation between the three territories, please provide us with useful information from your territory, by courier, so that we can start an action at a given time as agreed with you". My question about this, Mr. Bogilovic, is: Can you agree with me that this document shows that there were many units in the broader Srebrenica area, such as Pobudje TO, Susnjari TO, Slatina TO and so on and so forth, units that were not present at the meeting in Bajramovici when an agreement was reached? Units that were not even aware that the Srebrenica staff had come into existence?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I see this document. I have never been to Pobudje in my life, nor was I aware of this. The truth is, the villages, all the villages were compelled to come together and take certain decisions on what to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I hate to interrupt you but this question you had already asked during the first session and it had already been answered by the witness who confirmed what happened in Bajramovici was not known amongst -- in other areas, so I don't think you need to stress the point any further.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Your Honour. I wanted to ask a different question about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document also shows, Mr. Bogilovic, does it not, that these groups acted of their own accord and independently of each other, is that true?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not only this group, there were other groups too.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic. May we have a number for this document, please, the 6th of June, 1992 document from Pobudje to be assigned a number as a Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. D237.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document will become Defence Exhibit D237.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to show the witness a different document. This time this is 00926448. This is a Kragljevode TO staff document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, can you have a look, please. This document was produced by the Kragljevode TO staff, the number is 04/92, the date is 25th of June, 1992. The document was signed by commander major Begovic, a person you have referred to. The document is entitled: "Order", and then "pursuant to the decision of the BH Presidency, and the commander of the BH Territorial Defence, I hereby declare a state of general mobilisation". My question is, you will agree with me, Mr. Bogilovic, will you not, that the TO staff commander of Kragljevode on the 25th of June, 1992, refers to a decision made by the BH Presidency and the commander of the territorial defence of BH, but certainly makes no reference to the Srebrenica staff, does he? Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These local groups, will you agree, will you not, helped each other out on occasion, whenever necessary, whenever local commanders saw it fit?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite true. They had to communicate by courier and the villages helped each other out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They help helped each other out whenever local commanders saw fit, is that true? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Or whatever they agreed to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a number for this exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document will become Defence Exhibit D238.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next, I would like the usher to show the witness OTP Exhibit 150. 150. This is a document of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the command of the Drina division. The date is the 1st of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The number for this document is 02110288. Mr. Bogilovic, can you please have a look now. I will quote from this document. It says: "Pursuant to an oral orders by the Srebrenica commander, 7.62 millimetre ammunition must be collected, 5.000 bullets. I hereby order that company commanders and front line commanders carry out an assessment of the situation along the front lines. They shall be responsible to take ten bullets from each of their soldiers. If any ammunition is collected, it is then to be taken back to Srebrenica". You would agree with me, would you not, that this document indicates that the order is by the Srebrenica commander, whereas to be assessed on the spot by company commanders and front line commanders so that then would they decide what to do. Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had never seen this document until it was shown to me by the OTP. Therefore, I can hardly comment whether it is authentic or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, I didn't ask you about the document's authenticity. What I would like you to comment on is, if you know anything about the substance of this document. What I've just read out to you, what the document says, that the commanders themselves should assess the situation along the lines, and that they were the ones responsible for deciding. Does that not show that the Srebrenica commanders order was left to local -- to the local commanders to assess. Is that true, or not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's precisely what the document appears to say. It is not ordered. It is said that the commanders should make an assessment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also, what they say about any ammunition that might be collected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I don't know when we're reading from the English, where we have anything they have to make an assessment about whether to follow the order. What I do see in the English version is that the company and line commanders evaluates the situation along the lines and at their own responsibility to take ten bullets from each soldier. Now, unless that is a characterisation that Defence has given, I just want to make that -- well, actually ask that question and make it clear because that is not what is translated on the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will again do what I did a while ago, but before I go on, Your Honour, something we have noticed in many documents, especially the war log, the war diary -- which will be used again and again throughout this trial -- there seem to be many mistranslations concerning essential points. Therefore, if I may bring up a suggestion, the OTP should maybe have these translations checked. And the same applies to many other documents. I do not wish to discuss this in front of the witness now, but I will again ask for this document to be placed on the ELMO so that the interpreter can follow what I'm saying or just interpret on their own. The Bosnian version reads as follows: "I hereby order the company commanders and front line commanders to assess the situation along the front lines and add their own responsibility, take ten bullets from each of the soldiers. Any ammunition collected in this way is to be taken to Srebrenica", and that's what the text says, that's what I've shown the witness. Witness, have you been able to follow?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that not precisely what it says?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Assessment. If they assess or evaluate the situation, then they should do it. If their assessment is to the contrary, then they shouldn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I have a different question for you now, in relation to this. Prior to that, can we please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. It's just confirming that it is already in the record here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another question about this, Witness. What about your information, does it not show that many orders by the Srebrenica staff were treated like this in practice? That's in as far as you know.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably so, because all the other units in the other areas made decisions too, in other municipalities, what they should do, especially in Bratunac municipality, which had its own structure. Once they had fled Bratunac, they organised themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that in practical terms, more was being done in terms of cooperation between these armed groups and staffs, rather than work carried out concerning the chain of command or lines of subordination. You as a police officer must know what that means?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Can you please explain that to me, lines of subordination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, that in practice, more was done, in terms of cooperation between these armed groups than in terms of orders being sent down from the staff to the units on the ground.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's quite true. The greatest -- the greatest problem was the logistics. And the greatest effort was being made about the logistics, about the people being hungry and that was the paramount problem they had at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I reading you correctly, are you trying to say that the staff was in no position to secure the logistics and, therefore, had no influence on the troops on the ground?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely. No one could influence them, not the Presidency, not the staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's true, isn't it, that throughout 1992, Oric was in no position at all, was entirely unable to affect the appointment of local commanders, since they were selected and appointed by the local population? Would I be right in claiming that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, entirely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance yet again please. I would like to show the witness another exhibit. This is a noted P exhibit, P75. This is a decision of the TO staff, an alleged decision of the Srebrenica TO staff, number 3/92 of the 26th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, please take a look at it and I will read to you the statement of reasons. "The Srebrenica TO staff shall be expanded with new members who are organisers of armed resistance against the aggressor in the territory of Srebrenica municipality from areas with no representatives in the staff which was formed on the 20th of May, 1992". Mr. Bogilovic, in connection with this, I will ask you the following, pursuant to this document, it seems that the staff functioned according to the principle of representatives of villages or areas and you confirmed this, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In the same way that Zulfo, Akif and Oric were chosen, the others were also chosen in their villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
