utterances.text: Thank you. These were not professionals with military training who could deal with issues which command bodies such as the TO staff would be competent to deal with?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. I saw that young boy, Nedzad Bektic, for the first time. He was in some kind of military school and he ran away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The others who were chosen in Bajramovici and the ones with which the staff was expanded, none of them had the necessary military training?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way. Some were policemen. One was a physical education teacher. Zulfo was a farmer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These areas chose the men they trusted, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct that Oric could not even influence the selection of his own associates?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he couldn't. First of all, he didn't know the areas or the people outside and of course he couldn't affect the nominations or the selection of the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It's also correct that Ustic and Tursonovic, in their areas, in the course of 1992 and later in the first months of 1993, continued to have their own independent commands, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Ustic, not in 1993. He was killed before that. But Zulfo always kept that for himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You wanted to say that Zulfo Tursonovic, throughout 1992, up until the demilitarisation in 1993, had an independent command in the area of Suceska?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's also correct, is it not, that Akif Ustic, until he was killed, also had an independent command?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He was a little arrogant. I'm sorry he's not alive because one shouldn't speak badly of those who are dead, but that's what he was like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now put a question to you. And based on what you saw and based on your experiences in Suceska, please tell us, even if Oric during 1992 and part of 1993 had wanted to replace Zulfo Tursunovic, he could not have done that, could he?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise. It calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not necessarily. Let's see whether he can answer that question. And if he can answer that question, on what ground he reaches that conclusion, whichever that conclusion will be. I don't want you to speculate, Mr. Bogilovic. If you know the answer to that question, you give it to us. If you don't know the answer, you tell us you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm 99 per cent sure he couldn't have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason for that, Mr. Bogilovic, is because the people of Suceska would not have accepted that, am I right?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the people who appointed him. He came from among the people of Suceska. Nobody from the outside appointed him. And by his nature, Zulfo was -- well, there's information about him showing what he was like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You wanted to say that Zulfo was a difficult man, wasn't he? A short-tempered man?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In his village, everybody knew him and they trusted him, because they elected him their leader.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Would the usher now please show the witness P42, that is Prosecution Exhibit P42. This is a decision of the War Presidency of the first of July 1992, whereby the War Presidency was established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, could you please pay attention to the names of the members of the War Presidency. I will ask you something about that. Under 8, Mirsad Dudic and, 11, Senahid Tabakovic. You knew those men, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct, is it not, that Mirsad Dudic and Senahid Tabakovic were local commanders of military units?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Dudic Mirsad in Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Osmace? Yes. And as commanders of local units, they were members of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. Because these were the first people who were there when it was established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. So the situation was such that they, as commanders of units, were supposed to be subordinated to Oric, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because if they were holding posts in the army, then they should have been under the command of the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that as members of the Presidency, which was the supreme command, they were, to say the lease, his equals, or rather, his superiors. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They all had the same voting rights if a ballot was taken and none of them could cast two ballots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think you answered my question. As members of the War Presidency, which was the supreme command, to say the least, they were Oric's equals, and moreover, they were his superiors because they were members of the War Presidency. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On their own territory they had equal rights to make decisions, just as Oric did because they carried out decisions in their own villages and it was they who actually made the decisions in their own villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Would the usher now, please, show the witness another document. This is document P109.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Make sure that you put them all on the ELMO, usher, please, because these were not prepared for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, would you please look at this document. This decision number 11/92 allegedly issued by the Municipal Staff of Srebrenica. Would you please look at the title carefully. It says, "Subject, decisions of the Territorial Defence Staff Srebrenica". When asked by the Prosecutor on Friday about this, you said that you had attended a meeting on the 1st of July, 1992 when the decisions mentioned in this document were taken. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct, is it not, that at that time it was first -- the War Presidency that was elected first and then it issued the decision on establishing the military police and the appointing Mirzet Halilovic. Would you please look at paragraph 2 of this document. It says: "The war military police is established hereby and Mirzet Halilovic was appointed the commander of this unit". Am I correct in saying that the War Presidency issued a decision establishing the military police and appointing Mirzet Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct that on the first of July, 1992 the War Presidency was established. And the members of the War Presidency then appointed these individuals, Mirzet Halilovic, Alic, Hamid.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to raise a point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I think there has been, within the question -- even though Mr. Bogilovic has continued to answer, I think there has been a mischaracterisation in the evidence that was presented. There was evidence from the Prosecution where Mr. Bogilovic was shown a document dating from the 15th of June that showed an appointment of the military commander and then this document chronologically did come afterwards. He said that he did not have knowledge of that other document or was present there. So right now, I don't think we can characterise that it was clear that the first the Presidency was established and then Mirzet Halilovic was appointed. There has been evidence to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What do you have to say about that, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not understand the objection raised by the Prosecutor, but my question is quite clear. I said, In view of the fact that Mr. Bogilovic attended this session, he knows precisely what happened there. I asked him whether the War Presidency was elected and whether, after its election, it proceeded to appoint, or rather, to establish the military police and appoint Mirzet Halilovic. This is something that the witness can explain very simply because he attended the session. I don't see how the witness could not know this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But what are you trying to prove at the end of the day? That Mirzet Halilovic was appointed by the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's stick to that. Was Mr. Halilovic appointed as commander of the military police by the War Presidency or by someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Zulfo Tursunovic proposed that Mirzet Halilovic be the member of the military police on the 1st of July, 1992 when the War Presidency was formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was, not who nominated him, but who appointed him?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did. The members of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the War Presidency. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was covered in a previous question. It's already -- I mean, we have already covered that. So if we can try, please, to avoid repetitions, we will finish earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, it would be wrong to claim that Naser Oric on the 1st of July, 1992 appointed anyone, including Mirzet Halilovic. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He certainly couldn't have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that this document, which has been shown to you, is, in fact, information passed on by Oric to the republican TO staff?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't go into that, because on that day I was wounded, when this was drafted, on the 2nd of July. And how he could have passed this on when there were attacks on that day, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you agree that this kind of document, which is entitled "Decisions of the TO Staff of Srebrenica" could be simply a clumsy formulation by someone?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I agree you don't even need to finish your sentence, Ms. Sellers. It's -- you either withdraw the question or reformulate it, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, in connection with this, I will rephrase my question. The expression used for the military police, is it rukovodilac, meaning something like manager, or komandir, commander?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be komandir, in practice, commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that it would be unprofessional to say that rukovodilac, the leader of the military police?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's an unprofessional expression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I will move on now. During your testimony on Friday, you said that the president of the War Presidency, Mr. Hajrudin Avdic, called you on the 14th of October, 1992 and he said: "From today on Mirzet Halilovic is under your command". Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. I received this in writing, dated the 14th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you agree with me then that the War Presidency, putting the commander of the military police under your authority was, in fact, commanding the military police in this way?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the signature on the document I received, that's what it says, because the document I received, that I had authority over the military police commander, this was signed by the president of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, this has been covered already, both during the in-chief and during your cross-examination. He was referred to this yesterday. Whether the fact that Halilovic was put under his command meant that the rest of the military police was also put under his command and I think he covered that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree. But there is another question that follows from the previous one, which I am about to ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Friday, the Chamber asked who Mr. Halilovic was subordinated to, on page 64 of the transcript, Friday's transcript, line 22 through 24 you answered: "According to the rule, he was subordinate to the army". Mr. Bogilovic, I entirely agree with you that according to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. rules, the military police was under the army's command. But will you agree with me that rules are one thing and what happens in -- what happened in the second half of 1992 and first half of 1993 in Srebrenica was in fact something entirely different?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, Mr. Bogilovic, at the time things didn't exactly go according to the rules in Srebrenica, did they?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no way they could have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance now. I would like to show the witness part of Exhibit P84. P84. It's the war log and the number of the page is 02115050.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's page 7 on the English text.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 7, yes. I will be showing some bits midway down the page, as well as the last paragraph. Mr. Bogilovic, if you can please have a look. You weren't able to read the handwriting, so I will now read it out to you. Just under "organisation and functioning." Just under "organisation and functioning of the civilian and military authorities in the free territory," it reads: "The meeting was called to order by Osman Osmanovic. He pointed out that we were facing problems regarding the functioning of the system. The War Presidency to staffs - civil protection". Ramiz then took the floor saying: "The War Presidency stands in for the Assembly", and then he enumerates the various tasks discharged by the War Presidency. And then just underneath he says: "Hierarchy." If you can have a look. This has been shown to you by the Prosecutor. "Reviews and assesses the war situation. Makes decisions. It is the supreme authority and the supreme command." Mr. Bogilovic, do you agree that what was being discussed at the time was the fact that the War Presidency was, in fact, the supreme authority, the supreme body and the supreme command. You were present, after all, were you not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I was there and this was precisely what was discussed and no one could tell which came first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now please look at the continuation, where it speaks about the War Presidency. It reads: "Command exercised through the staff. Direct command over the military police, but simultaneously the military police is subordinated to the armed forces staff". So my question would be, do you agree that what it says here is that the War Presidency is the direct commander of the military police?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, because the president gave me a copy of this decision that was signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When asked by the Prosecutor on Friday whether prior to being subordinated to Mirzet Halilovic was within the chain of command -- within the military chain of command, you answered yes.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, I put it to you that in the military, on the 14th in October 1992 in Srebrenica there was no complete military chain of command. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, because there were no proper authorities in place in order to set up a thing like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you said that in the army -- that the military police was in the army's chain of command, you meant that's what it should have been like, in terms of the regulations?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's precisely what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But in actual fact, even prior to the 14th of October, 1992, as well as after, at least until as long-- as late as the end of 1992, it was the War Presidency that exercised direct command over the military police. Was it not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was appointed on the 14th of October, I answered to the War Presidency, or rather, to Mr. Hajrudin. In view of the confusion and misunderstanding, I was supposed to submit my reports to Hajrudin and this is precisely what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that it was the War Presidency that took the decision to replace Mirzet Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think after I submitted the proposal, the command was involved too and it was a unanimous decision once everyone had been informed of the situation. The vote to replace Mirzet Halilovic - or suspend him, whichever way you like - was a unanimous decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, did you at any point find out that Mirzet Halilovic had been replaced on grounds of suspicion that a murder had been committed in the prison?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew nothing about that. I'm sorry not to have the document here now, because I had gathered quite some evidence about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you hear anything like this being said in connection with his removal or replacement?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nothing along these lines at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It's true, isn't it, that it was the War Presidency that took the decision to appoint Krdzic? You did see that decision yesterday, didn't you? You remember that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember. I did see it yesterday, but I'm unable to confirm this. The discussion was about who the replacement should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have to answer this one now, Mr. Bogilovic, because I will come back to this question and this document later on. Let me ask you a different question now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance please. I would like to show the witness another excerpt from the OTP's P84 and the page is 5057.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Page 12 and 13 of the English text.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a meeting of the Srebrenica armed forces staff and the date is 23rd of October, 1992. Mr. Bogilovic, since you have a hard time deciphering the handwriting, I will quote to you what it says under A1. Can you follow?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A letter sent from the Biljeg Battalion was read out requesting appropriate measures to be taken with regard to soldiers and civilians stirring trouble on the ground. A decision was taken to forward a decision on the soldiers to the military police in order to bring them in. And the civilian police will do the same in regard of civilians. First of all, Tihic Ah -- Ahmo must draw a distinction between soldiers and civilians. In relation to that I will ask you the following. It's true isn't it that throughout 1992 and the first month --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, you have to go to Page 13, bottom of Page 12 and the first part of page 13 and what's more important is on page 13, the top of page 13 and not what is on Page 12. Yes. Madam Vidovic, I apologize to you for the short interruption.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, it's true, isn't it, that throughout 1992 as well as the first months of 1993 most people in Srebrenica were entirely unclear about this distinction between civilians and soldiers. There was no clearcut separation between the two. People were not familiar with these terms in a formal sense, were they?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're quite right. A soldier would wear the same clothes as a civilian. It was difficult to tell. As for food, everyone would go to get food, men and women.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that this part of the transcript that I have read out to you claims that an order should be forwarded to the military police with regard to soldiers, four soldiers to be brought in and that the civilian police should be in charge of bringing in civilians. Forwarding an order is not quite the same thing as ordering the respective police forces to do something. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're entirely right. Both police forces should be -- should know what to do. If there was someone causing a public disturbance, obviously this person would have to be brought in and interrogated and take whatever steps could be taken. There were no courts, after all, to turn to at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, the essence of my question goes to the following. It is not quite the same thing to forward an order and to issue and order. Would I right in saying that if you can say?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Order and execution is the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But forwarding an order, can it be the same thing? And you were a police officer yourself so you should know, because you received orders and you passed orders on. If you pass on an order down the line from a superior command, sometimes it means nothing else. You just pass it on down the line to a subordinate command.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If an order was given to a commander then the commander would have been duty bound to carry it out. If he was tasked to carry out an assessment of the situation, it would have been entirely down to him and no one else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I asked you about passing on or forwarding an order. That is not the same as issuing an order.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite certainly so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please now look at the second to last sentence on the same page of the log book. It reads: "The conclusion is hereby adopted that an interview should be conducted with the military police commander at the staff in the presence of the commander regarding the functioning of the military police". Mr. Bogilovic, you occupied a leading position in the police force. Would it not have been entirely common or usual for a commander or any superior officer to simply issue an order to one of their subordinates to act in a certain way instead of holding an interview with that person. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of hierarchy, in terms of personnel, in terms of the chain of command, he should go and report to his first commander, then to his second commander. As for the rest, yes, I entirely agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we now show the witness an excerpt, a different one from P84. The page is 02115075. In English this is page 24 and 25. Mr. Bogilovic, we will now be showing you an excerpt from a meeting of the Srebrenica armed forces staff dated the 10th of November, 1992. Can you please have a look midway down the page, the first sentence, under the Roman numeral II. It reads -- if you turn -- it's two pages further on, you will see that these are minutes from the 10th of November session of the staff. 1992. These are minutes, just under the Roman numeral II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 25, usher, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 5075, the Bosnian version. We can give you a hand if you don't have it there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, can you check exactly which page the witness is reading from please. The ERN number. It is the right one? Yes. Do you see a Roman two, a big Roman two there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The sentence which starts immediately below that number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour. Right there. It says: "Cooperation with the military police is good".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bogilovic, at the staff meeting, cooperation with the military police is under discussion, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can the usher now please show the witness a different excerpt from P84. The page is 0215063. The relevant page in English is 16 and 17, are the page numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, please have a look. This is an excerpt from the minutes of a meeting of the staff held on the 3rd of November, 1992 which I will now quote from. I am quoting the bit that is just further down from "conclusions and proposals" so you have a meeting of the armed forces staff 3rd of November. Then it says, "conclusions and proposals" and then it says, "schedule a meeting of RP", of the War Presidency. It says here, "In addition to the members of the staff, B Ramiz shall also take part in the meeting of the Presidency. The meeting has now agenda as yet".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to have page 17, top of page 17 on the ELMO. It is? Okay. Can you start again, Madam Vidovic. You can start after that a meeting of the War Presidency should be convened.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "In addition to the chief of staff, the meeting of the War Presidency shall also be attended by B Ramiz. The meeting has no agenda, but it can be concluded from the announcement that the functioning of the two police forces will be discussed". My question, Mr. Bogilovic, is: It is quite obvious that it is the War Presidency that is about to discuss the functioning of the two police forces, both military and civilian. Would I be right in saying this?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, based on this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will read to you the last sentence of this part of the minutes with reference to the civilian and military police, "the staff thinks that staff changes are indispensable". You will agree with me, will you not, that the staff is only expressing its opinion and that it will be the War Presidency that will discuss both police forces?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to ask the usher to show the witness another excerpt from the war log, from document P84, page 02115071. And the relevant part in English is on pages 21 and 22 at the beginning, the first paragraph on page 22, in the English version. Mr. Bogilovic, this is an excerpt from a joint session of the War Presidency and the Territorial Defence staff of the 19th [sic] of November, 1992. I will quote what Mirzet says. "You gave me" -- can you find it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "You gave me a free hand for two months. Is that good? But somebody didn't like it, that the town had been put in order. People from Potocari, the new people that I got, were worse". In fact, Mr. Bogilovic, "Mirza" is Mirza Halilovic isn't he?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And here, he is saying that people from Potocari didn't want there to be order in the town. It seems that there was a conflict between him and the people from Potocari. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what he says here, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Naser Oric comes from Potocari, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I would like to have the transcript corrected. I believe this is a meeting from the 9th of November. I believe the transcript says the 19th of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is 9th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The meeting I confirm is the 9th of November. So this correct for all intents and purposes where, in the transcript, line 17 of page 61, there is indicated that it took place on the 19th of November which is wrong. A mistake. Yes, let's continue, please. Thank you, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, during your testimony, at one point, you said that you risked your life drawing up information about Mirzet Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that Mirzet Halilovic was a short-tempered person, who under the then prevailing conditions in Srebrenica, it was not possible to keep under control. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are. Because there was no structure to arrest him, try him and lock him up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now please show the witness another excerpt from the Prosecutor's document, P84. These are pages from 0215077 to 02115079. In the English version, these are pages 26 to 29. These are minutes from a session of the staff of the armed forces of the 22nd of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at the sentence that starts under the Roman numeral five. So please turn to page 2 and you will see the Roman numeral five. Underneath it says, I quote: "Osman reported on the position of the War Presidency regarding the reorganisation of the military police. A request was a dismissal of the commander was also read". Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you will then turn the page, please. Yesterday, during your testimony, you were shown this page and told that in the middle it says "Mirzet Halilovic's resignation is unanimously accepted". Mr. Halilovic [sic], what we have here are two different notes about the same fact. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Mirzet was dismissed, not that he resigned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So will you agree with me that there was a demand for his dismissal and that he was dismissed, not that he resigned?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says here he resigned, but in fact he was dismissed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at all the names listed here as having taken part in the discussion. Would you please look at them. Do you agree that Mirzet Halilovic did not attend this session so he couldn't have resigned?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Naser, Hamed. Take a good look, please.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Afdic, Zulfo, Osman. He did not participate in the discussion, according to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bogilovic, I will now ask you something else with reference to the military police. In fact what was referred to as the military police in Srebrenica during 1992 and early 19 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Vidovic, before you proceed with your next question. So referring you back to the sentence, that particular sentence in part 5 part five of the page that you were referred to. When it says that Osman reported the position of the RP regarding the reorganisation of the VP, which is the military police. And then "a request for the dismissal of the commander was also read." Whose request would that be? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am not sure that the translation into English is correct. Mr. Bogilovic please follow me. In the Bosnian version it says: "Osman reported on the position of the War Presidency about the reorganisation of the military police." He did not report to the War Presidency. He reported on the position of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My question has got nothing to do with that, Madam Vidovic. My question is regarding the reorganisation of the VP. I read it just for the sake of having read it to refer the witness to the two lines of that particular -- from that particular page. My question relates to the last part of that -- of those two lines. A request for the dismissal of the commander was also read. Whose request was read? Who had made that request? Is it your letter that you had referred to earlier on that was read? Or is it someone else's request for the dismissal of the commander that was read? Please try to remember, because this is very important. It seems that at that meeting we have established the following: Halilovic was not there. We have established also that Halilovic did not actually resign out of his own free will or sent any letter of resignation. But --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. With all due respect, I would like to say that I think the witness did not say that Halilovic was not there, that he did not participate, because his name was not listed as one of the people present. The other thing is I think we have to make it clear, I don't know whether Madam Vidovic has asked Mr. Bogilovic whether he was present at this meeting. We did go over that on direct testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's clear that. Was Halilovic present at this meeting or not? That you can recall. Yes, Mr. Bogilovic, you have to tell us. I mean, say, yes, no, I don't remember, whatever your answer --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. I know that Mr. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Halilovic did not resign either in writing or orally. I know that Mr. Halilovic was dismissed after a debate on his behaviour and his actions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But it also says here that a request for the dismissal of the commander was also read. Whose request was read? Was it your request? Was it your letter, the one that you said you wrote believing that you were actually also risking your life by writing such a letter? Was this the request that was read out during that meeting, or was it something else, somebody else's request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this was a request based on the evidence I had supplied and my letter. Most probably they had other information as well. This was a request read out by the staff, because Osman was in the staff. So it's their conclusion. So Osman was informing the others that Mirzet had been dismissed from his duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. I will give him back to you, I mean it's -- I don't have any further -- I would ask him, actually, who would have formulated that request for the dismissal. But I think he is suggesting it was Osman Osmanovic himself, that's if I read him well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, you were not present at that session, were you? So you are not sure who actually formulated the request.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a request by the staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now move on and ask you something about the military police. Mr. Bogilovic, what was referred to as the military police in Srebrenica at the time and what should have been the military police according to the regulations? The only thing they had in common was the name; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I had the same. I didn't have any other conditions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the military police unit was not complete until the end of 1992, it did not have the necessary equipment or professional personnel until the end of 1992 and even later?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think throughout the time I was there, up to the demilitarisation, it never had the legal or proper or professional organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now ask the usher to show the witness another excerpt from P87. This time it's page 02115086. I apologise, I said P84 [as interpreted]. Not P87. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And we are talking of pages 33 and 34 in English, the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three and 34.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, look at the end of the page, the bottom where there is the Roman numeral 4. And underneath you see that Akif Krdzic is speaking.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are minutes from a session of the staff of the 4th of December, 1992 and he says - I will quote briefly -"Akif Krdzic: The military police is not complete. Many have given up because of food and accommodation. There are no weapons (only two rifles and two pistols)." Mr. Bogilovic, the military police unit had only two rifles and two pistols and in the chaotic situation prevailing in Srebrenica in late 1992, do you agree that whoever commanded this military police, without weapons and without professional staff, it was unable to function?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's correct, it was unable to function, but all the other structures were also missing the fundamental conditions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree with your, Mr. Bogilovic. I will ask you something else now. The weapons that existed in Srebrenica were indispensable for the defence of the lines from breakthroughs by the Serbs. And this was a question of life and death in Srebrenica, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, should I move on now? Or perhaps we could have a break now, because I'm moving on to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You know that I don't interfere with either you or the Prosecution when it comes to this. We have seven minutes. If you don't think you can cover the next matter --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I can proceed, Your Honour. Thank you. One more document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can overstay by a couple of minutes and then we will replace those minutes later. It's up to you. If you would like to stop now, we will stop now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will proceed with the next document. I will now ask you something else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, is it not, that the so-called operative staff was established in September 1992. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I was on sick leave. Most probably it was. Osman Osmanovic was there, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now please show the witness an excerpt from P84, page 02115050. In English, it's pages 7 and 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, this is a session that was held on the 14th of October, 1992. You agreed on Friday that you were present, that your name is reflected in the minutes. I will now read out to you Osman Osmanovic said. It's just below the heading. He said: "We are facing problems of the functioning -- assist the War Presidency to staff civilian protection." [as interpreted] And then you went on to say, I quote: "Due to a lack of familiarity with the specific problems, we set up a war staff, a War Presidency and an operations staff. The decisions are not implemented that are made by any of these three different bodies." That is what you said, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And despite everything I would like to pause here, Your Honour, and perhaps have a break, because I'm moving on to something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's have a 25-minute break starting from now, which means we will restart between 10 to and five to one o'clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, before the break we spoke about what you had said at the session of the staff on the 14th of October, 1992. You mentioned that because people were not familiar with the problems, the war staff, the War Presidency and an operations staff were set up. Based on what recorded, it appears that in September and at least until the 14th of October, 1992 there were two staffs functioning at the same time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was away at the time, but if the problems remained unresolved, that would seem to suggest that something was wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that there were, in fact, two different staffs in parallel for a while at least?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two staffs? I believe one didn't know exactly what the purview was of the War Presidency and the staff respectively.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll ask you more questions about that, but can I now have P79 shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is purported to be a document by the operations staff of the armed forces of Srebrenica, number is 15/92. The date is the 19th of September, 1992. The document was signed by Osman Osmanovic. You saw the document yesterday. I will quote the first section of the first paragraph of this decision, where it says right there, under the heading "subject". It reads: "The chief of the operations staff of the armed forces of Srebrenica, Osman Osmanovic, in accordance with the decision of the War Presidency and given authorisations, proposes that the operations staff of the armed forces in Srebrenica consists of the following departments and persons". Names which I will not read out in order not to waste more time on this. Do you agree with me, Mr. Bogilovic, that in actual fact the chief of the operations staff, Osman Osmanovic, had the authority pursuant to a decision of the War Presidency to set up an operations staff, because that's what the document indicates, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is indeed true. Now, as to who he was subordinated to or who he was superior to, these are military rules and guidelines that I'm not familiar with. I wasn't then and I am not now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now read out part of this statement of reasons. It says here: "From the time of appointment as chief of the operations staff, I have worked on consulting the necessary personnel and departments following which I drew up a proposal of the above. I propose that the Presidency endorse this by a decision of their own and request that a decision be -- or a decision be taken by those in the relevant positions at the republican level. Mr. Bogilovic, do you not agree that this document shows that Naser Oric was, in fact, not consulted when these people were nominated?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this, I believe this is actually about Osman Osmanovic, the chief of the operations staff, and he runs the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you not agree that this is about communication between the chief of the operations staff and the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed that's precisely what it says, because he's the one informing the Presidency that they should inform the relevant authorities at the republican level, and proceeds to give their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, you touched on the subject a number of times what I'm about to ask you. It's true, isn't it, that the persons who were members of the War Presidency or one of the staffs were not familiar with the sort of problems involved in the proper functioning of these bodies?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 99.999 per cent, they had no idea, they weren't trained, they weren't qualified. All those who were qualified had already left by this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, most of these people were people with secondary education, some of them worked in schools as teachers prior to the outbreak of hostilities, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it should say team for the salvation of the people and certainly not military, but as there was a war on, we assumed the name "military", so there you have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you now please show the witness a page from the military log, P84, again, the page number is 02115050. I believe the witness already has the page before him. It should be the one he's looking at. Can he please look at -- I think the page number is 8 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, can you please have a look. We can see your name on that document, Becir, and then just further down the name Zulfo.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a sentence in the middle of this paragraph. He says, "There is no unified command in the army". Have you found that? What Zulfo is saying?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's in the middle of his contribution. I'm trying not to read the whole paragraphs out in order to save time. It says, "One of the staff's is dying. We have to cut these bodies down". I will read right from the beginning what Zulfo is say. Zulfo says, "It is us who is to blame for all this calamity".

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Prior to the break we looked at the paragraph above. We didn't look at the last sentence in the paragraph above. Because of the sentence you are pointing out now, I think it is in relationship to what was said in the last sentence in the previous paragraph, by Mr. Bogilovic and I think that maybe we should put that into context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. THE INTERPRETERS: [Interpretation] Microphone for the President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you found it, or not? It's at the bottom. The last four lines, more or less, of the page, after you finished --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we start with you, actually. What are the last words that, according to this document you see? A peoples court should be set up. The disorder was caused by the armed forces? Do you find it? Can you read it there?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can read it out to the witness, Your Honours, if you agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last two sentences, Mr. Bogilovic, "a peoples court should be set up. It's the armed forces who caused trouble". These are the last two sentences of your own contribution and then following from there -- have you got it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zulfo takes the floor and speaks. "It is us who is to blame for all this calamity. We in this room, we need a military court not a peoples' court. One of the staffs is dying and we must reduce these bodies. There is no unified command in the army". Then, if you could please turn to the next page, it's very much in the same context as the question that I am about to ask. On page 5051, still page 8 in English, Avdo speaks and I quote: "We must appoint people to positions in power. We must unify command and set up a court martial. We must appoint professionals to some of the departments". In connection with these quotes, let me ask you the following. It's true, Mr. Bogilovic, isn't it, that on the 14th of December, 1992, disunity of command was in fact debated?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's why I think they called a joint meeting, a joint session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that on the 14th of October 1992 the situation was, in fact, such that the staff was not in command of many, many groups that were actually on the ground. Is this something you can confirm?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can also confirm that Mr. Ustic left arbitrarily of his own free will, without consulting or asking anyone. He just scrammed and he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that Mr. Ustic went to take action on his own without consulting anyone?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But without food, without telling anyone, without taking any of the soldiers with him. He just left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These armed groups, even at this time I'm talking about October 1992, kept functioning for quite a long time after such as Zulfo's army, Akma's army, Hakija army, Naser's army and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The names remained the same throughout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the word of the local commanders, these groups, was what mattered on the ground?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were the chief order givers on the ground. They were appointed by the people, chosen by the people, and the people obeyed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now please look at the next page 5052, last four digits, page 9 in English. The war log. Midway down the page, Naser spoke. It's Naser Oric we're talking about, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Naser: What we should do about Hakija's unit? They refused to hand their snipers over to Zulfo and to go to Fakovici." And then Delic speaks: "You are sending us to another area which has not been reconnoitred. You haven't given us any ammunition, whereas we have given everyone everything that has been requested". Then Osman speaks. "Hakija, could have said immediately at the meeting whether he could go into action or not. Now he's trying to justify himself. They failed to comply with quite a lot of things. Quite a lot of things". Zulfo again: "I don't blame Hakija for not going into action. He had asked for volunteers for an ambush after my return from the action. I don't know whether it's true or not". And Naser speaks again: "Why isn't the waterworks being watched"? Mr. Bogilovic, in relation to what I just read out, this part of the minutes reflects the situation on the ground faithfully as it was at the time, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the ground and in the terms of the way individuals were organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It wasn't possible to do anything at all about the local commander who failed to comply with the terms of the agreement. Is that not right?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was not enough ammunition, was there?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite right. No ammunition, no clothes, no food, no blankets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was antagonism between various local commanders, was there not?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For a while they secured their own basic bodyguards for themselves. So the president of the municipality came to see me once asking to have one assigned too, but I refused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now please look at page 5051, halfway down the page it is Naser speaking again. I quote: "All the present problems were caused by issues to do with organisation. What it all boils down to is that each do their own work and you can have your petty quibbles about power later on. Please try to see some sense. We must organise ourselves. Dig in and save ourselves. Possibly there is more ammunition in Fakovici that has not been taken yet. If we aspire to be an army, there must be order and there must be a command". Mr. Bogilovic, Naser Oric tried very hard to bring some order to this whole situation, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a very composed person by nature. He liked peace and he liked order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, Mr. Bogilovic, isn't it, that he spoke about the same things on many other occasions that you're aware of, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now please look again at the same page. Osman Osmanovic is the chief of the operations staff, so I'm quoting his contribution to you. He says: "No society can function without authority, without bodies of government. It seems that some of us do not want [illegible], but rather to keep their own rules. We have a free territory and our own armed forces. We need to set up the proper authorities, a court, and just work on". Then Hamdija speaks. This is Hamdija Fejzic, a member of the War Presidency, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His name is stated as Hamdija.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just underneath Hajrudin Avdic's name, he says -- well, over here, when you have the positions enumerated, Mr. Bogilovic, I am right when I say that Hamdija was the president of the executive committee of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He said: "I do not agree that those who haven't even had a whiff of war should be included in the bodies of government. The head of the army and government must be someone whom people are ready to follow and not educated people. Based on this, let me ask you. This is a position put forward by Hamdija, a member of the War Presidency. Does it not reflect a more general feeling in Srebrenica at the time, that the army should be led, the army as well as the authorities, should be led by someone whom people are prepared to follow, not necessarily just educated people?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, it cannot in fact be claimed that all of this reflected Oric's position, or indeed, that this was something that he tried to impose on others at the time.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. By no means could you say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is clearly reflected in this war log -- and you have seen a number of sessions by now, Mr. Bogilovic -- is that very often staff sessions were attended by members of the War Presidency, the entire War Presidency or sometimes they would be represented by the chairman, the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. president.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On many occasions there were joint meetings that were held too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The War Presidency was adamant that a decision should be taken regarding actions and that actions should be reported. They insisted that they be informed about any actions taken. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because there was a logistical problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It is possible to ascertain that those people who were members either of the War Presidency or of the staff were not familiar with the real purview of activity of the War Presidency of the staff of the commander and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's quite true, and I believe we mentioned this a couple of times already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In actual fact, their authorities overlapped didn't they?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a state of chaos in terms of decision making, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance now, please, I would like to show the witness OTP Exhibit P14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is purported to be an order of the operation staff of the armed forces of Srebrenica dated the 22nd of December, 1992. I am quoting, Mr. Bogilovic. "Pursuant to the decisions reached at the meeting of the Srebrenica armed forces staff on the 22nd of December, 1992, the commander of the Srebrenica armed forces issues the following order". And underneath, "The 23rd of December, 1992, a meeting of the War Presidency on the Srebrenica armed forces staff is to be held at 1000 hours". Mr. Bogilovic, you have seen this decision before. Even assuming that Oric had written this or indeed someone else on his behalf, do you still agree that this decision reflects a lack of familiarity with the way the relationship between a superior and a subordinate works? Could you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I myself was puzzled by the fact that this body was now ordering that a meeting of the War Presidency be held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, can you confirm that Oric was not an arrogant person who imposed his own positions on the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By nature he was very taciturn. He spoke little. He mostly pointed out mistakes in order to improve work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One cannot say that he imposed his own viewpoints on the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will now show you another document. The number is 0178773. Please look at this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document was issued by the staff of the armed forces of Srebrenica on the 2nd of August '92 and it says, "decision", but please first look at the heading of the document where it says, "Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Municipal Staff of the armed forces, Srebrenica". And then, please, look at the signature underneath where it says, "President of the War Presidency, Hajrudin Avdic". You will agree with me, Mr. Bogilovic, that the heading is that of the staff and that the signature is that of the president of the War Presidency, Hajrudin Avdic. This confirms, does it not, that neither in the staff nor in the War Presidency did people know how to draw up documents properly? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this document is something I've seen here for the first time. I know these two men, Edhem and Sabahudin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, can you answer my question, please. Do you agree, please, that the heading is that of one body and the signature is that of the president of a different body. So do you agree with me that this shows that neither the War Presidency nor the staff, that is people working there, knew how to draw up documents properly?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I agree with you, because the introductory part should be confirmed by the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because there's something that calls for some explanation. In the English text, between the heading and the text, there is handwritten "EB MUP ministry of the interior/03/on copy/E-1- 15". I don't see anything on the B/C/S document that you've given us here. Is this a different document or what is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can explain this. The translator put in our marking under which we gave this document to the translation service. This is our mark which we put on the document when we gave it to the translators. It has nothing to do with the original document. I know that it is like our markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will be 239. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. D239. Defence Exhibit D239.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again there is another mistake, because I said D239, Defence Exhibit 239, not Ms. Vidovic. It appears that -- but what I was saying was being said by Ms. Vidovic. Let's proceed anyway because we have corrected it. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, it's correct, is it not, that the War Presidency and the staff interfered in each other's fears of competence?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, because they didn't know who was senior and who was junior among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. There were no regulations, instructions. Am I right, no guidelines?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The War Presidency itself did not issue any instructions on the functioning of the staff and the conditions of war. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not enact any statute or a rule book or anything of the sort. We didn't know how to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. From Tuzla or Sarajevo, until the demilitarisation, did any of you receive any instructions or regulations. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the SUP was concerned, certainly not. And if I didn't receive any such thing, neither did anybody else. Because I never saw any rules of procedure arriving anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will now move on to another topic. The security tasks in the staff were first mentioned in October 1992. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was when Osman came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You said that on the 14th of October, 1992, the staff gained its security assistance in the form of Hamid Salihovic. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was no such person until then.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will now ask the usher to show the witness Prosecution Exhibit P221. The ERN number is 03721495.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, would you please look at the document. This is a decision of the appointment of Hamed Salihovic as chief for intelligence and security affairs?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is signed by the president of the War Presidency, Mr. Hajrudin Avdic. Would you please now look at item 5. Look at Roman numeral five.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says, "The decision shall take affect on the day of its adoption and the nominated and appointed person shall be obliged to report immediately to the chief of staff of the armed forces". And the next sentence reads, "The appointed person shall be directly accountable for his work to the chief of staff of the armed forces". It's correct, is it not, that the chief of staff of the armed forces was Osman Osmanovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, this means that if he sent any reports, Hamed Salihovic as chief for security, was duty bound to deliver these to Osman Osmanovic as his direct superior. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, would the usher please show the witness another excerpt from P84, the war diary. This time page 02115065. These are English pages 17 and 18. This is the minutes of a session of the staff of the 7th of November 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, please look at Roman numeral two and I quote what it says here in Roman numeral two. "Hamed Salihovic, a member of the staff, submitted an oral report on the visit of some commanding officers to Konjevic Polje and Cerska from the first to fifth of November 1992. During that period, a series of meetings was held in the free territories of the municipalities of Zvornik, Vlasenica and Bratunac. At the meetings, it was concluded by the representatives of the municipalities, and confirmed by the above municipalities, Srebrenik, Bratunac, Vlasenica, Zvornik, that they should be merged into a subregion. The War Presidency of the subregion, the commander of its armed forces and its armed forces operations staff were elected. "What remains is for the War Presidency of Srebrenica to ratify these decisions. Our commander up to now, Naser O, has been elected commander of the armed forces of this subregion. "Our staff members, Hamid S and Hazim Dz were elected to the following posts: Hamid S was elected president of the War Presidency, that is, for the president of the War Presidency". Mr. Bogilovic, I will ask you the following question about this. S Hamid, is that Hamed Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the staff of the armed forces in Srebrenica, there was no other Hamid S, was there? Other than Hamed Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Hamed Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bogilovic, let us know leave aside the fact of whether the subregion was ever put into practice or not. But it's true, is it not, that in early November 1992, Hamed Salihovic was fully engaged and busy in the attempts to establish the subregion and to unify the command. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the creation of the subregion, I did not participate in this and I was not involved, but I did find out that Hamed Salihovic was in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. From the 1st of November onwards, he was in Konjevic Polje and Cerska when he was appointed to the War Presidency of the subregion?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of his movements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that at that time, from November 1992 onwards, Cerska and Konjevic Polje were in a very difficult situation because of Serb attacks?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that. It was constantly on the news. And there were constant appeals for assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hamed Salihovic was very busy. He had his hands full trying to unify the army. He wrote appeals to the authorities of Tuzla, Bosnia-Herzegovina, the international community and so and so forth. Did you hear about this?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a literate man and this probably got on someone's nerves. He was literate compared to the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't you think that he was doing this because he had been appointed president of the War Presidency of the subregion and it was in that capacity that he was attempting to do something?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well probably, yes. But as the number 1 person, he should have had the necessary resources.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will now ask the usher to show the witness one other document, P177.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a decision of the War Presidency of the subregion. Could you please take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If this decision is authentic, it reads as follows -- I quote: "The War Presidency of the subregion of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica and Zvornik municipalities and the staff of the subregion armed forces at the joint meeting held on the 7th of February 1993 Konjevic Polje Bratunac municipality passed the following decision. "In case the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the general staff of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina do not implement the decisions of the Presidency of the subregion and the staff of the subregion armed forces of the 7th of February 1993, that municipality will organise itself politically with a view to survival in this area of these territories. And the decision shall take effect on the date of its adoption." Mr. Bogilovic, if this document is authentic, it would appear that the War Presidency of the subregion around the 7th of February 1993, had very serious problems in this area. Do you agree that the situation was very difficult on the 7th of -- around the 7th of February, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree about the situation that it was very difficult. It was more than difficult. As for what is written here, I cannot testify about it because I have never seen this before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. If this document is authentic, the president of the War Presidency, Salihovic was evidently dealing with major political issues such as the political organisation of the municipalities in the subregion. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because in the elections he was among the leading people in the party and this is probably what irritated people and why he continued working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I am now rounding off this topic. This might be a good time to break. I am very far advanced in my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. That is what we will do and we will also give a well deserved rest to the witness. Tomorrow will be your last day here, Mr. Bogilovic. In the meantime, you will be escorted out of the courtroom by Madam Usher. Please rest so that you will come here fresh tomorrow morning at 9.00 when we restart. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9 o'clock. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
